key_insight: QOC-Workbench uses an LLM as an autonomous quantum co-scientist to design hardware-compliant control protocols across multiple quantum control paradigms, not just tune parameters.
engineering_relevance: The workflow can reduce expert effort and produce practical control schedules, auxiliary fields, and catalysts that better fit real hardware constraints.
method: Parses physics literature and proposes structural hypotheses for control design.
Writes simulation code to validate candidate protocols automatically.
Builds cross-task control motifs and, for counterdiabatic driving, learns amortized coefficient generators with a graph neural network.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful demonstrations in three settings, with Case 1 and 2 outperforming literature baselines and Case 3 transferring learned control paths to larger unseen systems.
watch_item: Because the workflow depends on literature parsing, code generation, and simulation validation, reliability and reproducibility will hinge on careful auditing of each autonomous step.
paper_title: LLM-Driven Cross-Paradigm Design for Quantum Optimal Control
